backlog.spec: Count consecutive restarts that did not improve the best radius sum by more than 1e-7. When the count reaches 12, empty the pool (the global best is kept separately in `best` and is still returned at the end), reset the counter, and let the search rebuild a new pool from fresh random starts and their crossovers. Do not do a reset when less than 25% of the search time is left. No other change. The aim is to stop a seed that has converged to a second-rate basin from spending the rest of its time on children of that basin.
backlog.title: Stagnation-triggered pool reset

backlog.spec: For 25% of restarts once the pool is non-empty, take the best pool packing and pick a random pair of touching circles (gap < 1e-4) whose radii differ by at least 20%. Swap their radii and then shrink both to 0.9 times their new values so that the start is closer to feasible. Use the resulting (centres, radii) as x0 for _solve_once. Do not jitter anything else. This is a minimal topology change in the size arrangement, distinct from jitter or relocation.
backlog.title: Radius swap moves between unequal neighbours

backlog.spec: In _cross, when the child has fewer than n circles, do not add circles at uniformly random positions with radius 0.05. Instead add them one at a time at the point of largest clearance among 500 uniformly sampled candidate points, where clearance = min(distance to walls, distance to each existing child centre minus its radius), with radius max(0.01, 0.9 * clearance). When the child has more than n circles, do not delete at random: repeatedly delete the circle with the largest total overlap with the others (sum of max(0, r_i + r_j - d_ij)), breaking ties by the smallest radius. The rest of the script is unchanged.
backlog.title: Hole-filling for missing circles in crossover

backlog.spec: In _cross, before cutting, apply a random element of the dihedral group of the square to each of the two parent packings (a random choice among the 8 symmetries: swap x and y, and/or flip x and/or flip y, mapping centres into [0,1]^2 and keeping radii). This lets the vertical cut combine different orientations of good packings. Everything else (cut position, filling, pool update) stays as before.
backlog.title: Dihedral transform of pool members before crossover

backlog.spec: In the penalty-energy relaxation of fresh starts, draw a per-start target radius uniformly from [0.07, 0.11] for all circles. Then start SLSQP with radii set to 0.8 times the target. This diversifies the basins reached by fresh starts. Keep pool of 5 and the rest as in slot 11.
backlog.title: Penalty relaxation with randomised target radius

backlog.spec: Replace the strict elitist pool update with a Metropolis rule. A new packing with radius sum S_new enters the pool if it is among the top 5 or, with probability exp((S_new - S_worst)/T), replaces the worst member, where S_worst is the smallest sum in the pool and T is 0.005 times the sum of the best member. Keep the best packing returned separately so the final answer is always the best ever found. Use rng for the acceptance draw.
backlog.title: Metropolis acceptance into the elite pool

backlog.spec: In the penalty relaxation of fresh starts, give each circle its own target radius from a mixture: 8 circles at about 0.13, the other 24 at about 0.075, with the large circles chosen at random. Relax the centres by L-BFGS-B against the sum of squared overlaps of the target radii, then run SLSQP with these target radii as the initial radii. Compare with equal targets.
backlog.title: Size-mixed relaxation targets

backlog.spec: In _cross, before the cut, apply an independently chosen random symmetry of the square to each parent. There are 8 (identity, rotations by 90/180/270 degrees, reflections in x=0.5, y=0.5 and both diagonals), implemented as coordinate maps on the centres; radii are unchanged. This lets the left part of one optimum combine with differently oriented parts of another. Leave everything else in _cross and solve unchanged.
backlog.title: Symmetry-transformed parents in crossover

backlog.spec: For 40% of the fresh starts (once the pool is non-empty), take the sorted radius vector of the best pool packing and multiply it by 0.97. Randomly permute these radii over n uniform random centres in [0.1, 0.9]^2. Relax only the centres with scipy L-BFGS-B (maxiter 150) on E = sum over pairs max(0, r_i + r_j - d_ij)^2 + sum over circles of max(0, r_i - x_i)^2 + max(0, r_i - y_i)^2 + max(0, x_i + r_i - 1)^2 + max(0, y_i + r_i - 1)^2, using the analytic gradient and bounds [0, 1] on the coordinates. Pass the relaxed centres and these radii as x0 to _solve_once. Other starts stay as they are now. Use the solve rng for all randomness.
backlog.title: Best-radius-profile restarts with penalty relaxation

backlog.spec: For 30% of the restarts once the pool has at least 1 member, pick a random pool packing and count each circle's contacts: neighbours or walls with gap < 1e-6. Choose one random circle among those with at most 2 contacts. If there is none, choose the smallest circle. Move its centre to the best of 500 random points, the one with the largest clearance to all other circles and the walls. Set its radius to 0.5 times that clearance, and use the result as x0 for _solve_once. This replaces some crossover starts, and the pool logic is unchanged.
backlog.title: Rattler relocation by contact count

backlog.spec: Change _cross only. Before combining the two parents, apply one of the 8 symmetries of the square (identity, 3 rotations about (0.5, 0.5), 4 reflections) chosen uniformly at random to parent b's centres, and with probability 0.5 swap the x and y columns of both parents so that the cut is horizontal instead of vertical. Then do the existing cut at t in [0.3, 0.7], including the existing trimming or random filling to n circles. This lets the crossover combine a good left half of one packing with a good top, bottom or mirrored half of another instead of only matching x-ranges. Everything else stays the same.
backlog.title: Symmetry-aligned crossover with random cut axis

backlog.spec: For fresh starts only (not crossover children): run _solve_once on n + 2 circles with maxiter 80 (make the circle count and maxiter arguments of _solve_once, uniform random start as now). Then delete the 2 circles with the smallest radii from the result and run SLSQP again on the remaining n circles from that point with MAX_ITER iterations. The repair step, the pool and the time loop work on the n-circle result as before. The extra circles let the solver decide which positions are useless before they are removed, which should give better n-circle arrangements than starting with exactly n. Check that one fresh start still finishes well within the time budget so that the 45 s limit is never reached.
backlog.title: Over-seed with n+2 circles, then drop the two smallest

backlog.spec: Since penalty-relaxed starts begin near feasible, run SLSQP with MAX_ITER 100 first. If the resulting radius sum is within 0.01 of the best in the pool, continue with SLSQP warm-started for 200 more iterations. This frees time for more restarts. Use slot 11 relaxation for fresh starts.
backlog.title: Smaller MAX_ITER for relaxed starts with adaptive extension

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, drop the final r block from the constraint vector in cons. Instead pass SLSQP bounds: centres in [0, 1] and radii in [0, 0.5]. This removes n inequality constraints and keeps the variables in the box during iterations, which should give fewer iterations per solve and more restarts. Keep the remaining constraints and the rest of the code unchanged. _repair still guarantees validity.
backlog.title: Remove radius-nonnegativity constraints and use bounds

backlog.spec: Two changes to how SLSQP start points are made. (a) Fresh starts: draw centres uniformly in [0.1, 0.9]^2, then relax the centres only with scipy L-BFGS-B (maxiter 60, bounds [R, 1-R]) on the energy E = sum over pairs of max(0, 2R - d_ij)^2 with a fixed target radius R = 0.09, using an analytic gradient. Pass the relaxed centres with radii 0.05 to SLSQP. (b) Replace _cross by a relocation move: copy a random pool member, pick one circle with probability proportional to 1/radius, move its centre to the point of largest clearance among 400 uniformly sampled candidate points (clearance = min of wall distance and distance to the other centres minus their radii), set its radius to max(0.01, 0.9 * clearance), and use that as x0. Keep the 70% pool-move / 30% fresh split, the pool of 5, the repair step and the time loop unchanged.
backlog.title: Penalty-relaxed fresh starts plus relocation moves

backlog.spec: Once the pool is non-empty, build fresh starts (the 30% non-crossover branch) from the size distribution of the best pool member instead of equal radii 0.05: take its radius vector, multiply by 0.85, sort descending, and place the circles one at a time, largest first, at a uniformly sampled centre that does not overlap already placed circles and stays inside the walls (up to 200 tries per circle; on failure keep the last sample). Pass these centres and radii to SLSQP as x0. Before the pool has a member, keep the current uniform start. The aim is to explore new arrangements while keeping a size mix known to score well.
backlog.title: Fresh starts with radii copied from the best packing

backlog.spec: Per restart, generate 8 random starts, relax each with a short penalty L-BFGS-B (target radius 0.09), and send only the one with lowest final penalty energy to SLSQP. The relaxation is cheap compared with SLSQP, so SLSQP is spent on the most promising starts. Keep the pool of 5 and crossover as is.
backlog.title: Batch screening of relaxed starts by penalty energy

backlog.spec: Replace the single penalty relaxation of fresh starts with 3 successive L-BFGS-B stages (30 iterations each), where target radius grows 0.06, 0.08, 0.095 with warm-started centres. Then run SLSQP with radii set to 0.9 times the final target. This gives a gentle compression that avoids jamming early.
backlog.title: Annealed inflating penalty relaxation

backlog.spec: After repair, polish each packing with a cheap greedy growth pass. Visit circles in a random order drawn from rng. For each circle, set its radius to the largest value allowed by the walls and by the current radii of its neighbours (min over j of dist(i,j)-r_j, and walls). Repeat the sweep 5 times, stopping early if the sum stops changing by more than 1e-12. Apply this to the final best packing and to each pool member before it is stored. Use exact double-precision arithmetic and keep SHRINK at 1e-9 so the harness check still passes.
backlog.title: Coordinate-wise greedy radius growth polish

backlog.spec: Add a third kind of start, used for 30% of restarts once the pool has 2 members (then 50% crossover, 20% fresh). Take a random pool member, choose an axis (x or y) at random and a band [a, a + w] on the other coordinate with w uniform in [0.2, 0.4] and a uniform in [0, 1 - w]. Shift every circle whose centre lies in the band by the same offset delta along the chosen axis, delta uniform in [-0.08, 0.08], clip the centres to [r, 1 - r], multiply all radii by 0.95, and run SLSQP from that point. Sliding a whole row against its neighbours changes the stacking between rows, a structured move that jitter and single-circle moves cannot make.
backlog.title: Band-slide mutation of pool members

memo:
Helped: slot 0, a pool of the 5 best packings with SLSQP restarts from perturbed pool members (-2.9334, the only accepted change). Penalty-energy L-BFGS-B relaxation of fresh starts is the strongest signal: slot 11 gave -2.9396 on both of 2 runs, and slot 32 (noisy lattice or random starts, relaxed) also gave -2.9396/-2.9396. Slot 38 gave -2.9396/-2.9386. Diverse pool of 12 with the 1e-3 filter also helped (slot 18 -2.9386/-2.9349, slot 9 -2.9368), as did relocation (slot 29 -2.9396/-2.9360).
Did not help: schedule/time-fraction tuning (slots 1-6, within noise sd 0.0034), basin-hopping jitter (-2.9323), boundary-circle init (-2.9300), drop-and-resample (-2.9307), smallest-circle reinsertion (-2.9237), LP repair (-2.9297), multi-stage or reduced-constraint SLSQP (as low as -2.9044), analytic gradients (no change).
Next: adopt slot 11 as the base (-2.9396 replicated). Combine it with the pool of 12 and the 1e-3 filter, then add relocation. Avoid schedule tuning, large perturbations and repeating aborted ideas.
